q: Conway's Game of Life is Turing-complete. This means the halting problem for Life configurations is:
opts: Undecidable (no algorithm can decide for all initial configurations whether a given pattern eventually dies out)
Decidable because the grid is finite
exp: Since Life simulates Turing machines, the question 'does configuration C eventually become all-zero?' is at least as hard as the halting problem — undecidable. This is a dynamical systems statement: long-run behaviour of a cellular automaton is undecidable.
